$comment: SoPhy project settings. TRACKED IN GIT deliberately: the skills, agents and hooks are
part of the toolkit, reviewable in a diff, and there is exactly ONE copy — SoEEDF/.claude
is a symlink to this directory, so both roots resolve the same files (G1).
Machine-specific grants belong in .claude/settings.local.json, which is gitignored.
THE HOOKS. Each corresponds to a failure already paid for, and each names the CORRECT
action rather than only refusing. They are tiered: guard-generated-files.sh BLOCKS an edit
to a file that something demonstrably overwrites (it tests for the overwriting mechanism,
never for the path shape — verification/ beds keep hand-authored system/fvSolution and 0/
and must not be caught), and WARNS without blocking on the heuristic cases. guard-bash.sh
blocks `git add -A`/`.` per rule D4. session-start.sh only prints.
Every event, blocked or warned, is appended to .claude/hook-events.log so the set can be
tuned from evidence — /save-state reports what fired. If a BLOCK was wrong, that entry gets
ESCAPE HATCHES: `touch .claude/hooks-off` disables every hook while the file exists
(`rm` re-enables); or say so and the action is taken another way. No JSON editing to get
unstuck — a guard you cannot turn off quickly is a guard that gets deleted permanently.
